title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线，是 AI 从“能不能做”转向“怎么真正被用起来”：产品要把复杂度藏起来，agent 要进入真实工作流，基础设施要开始管理数据、模型与权限，而 builder 也得警惕所有人最后做出同一种东西。最值得记住的不是某个新 demo，而是这些变化背后的共同要求：让 AI 更容易用，也让人的判断更不能被省略。

archive.title: AI 落地日报
archive.desc: 从 AI 产品的易用性、agent 工作流到基础设施与创作者判断力，今天的 feed 都在追问同一件事：如何让 AI 真正进入日常。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-10-05 source feeds.

sections.title: AI 产品先要把复杂度藏起来 / Products Need to Get Out of the Way
sections.desc: 今天的 adoption 难题，很多时候不是模型不够强，而是产品把太多控制杆直接丢给了用户。

rewrite: Madhu Guru argues that AI adoption is largely a product problem. Even among the small share of people paying for AI, usage remains shallow because many products feel like airplane cockpits, with connectors, permissions, model choices and token usage all exposed at once.
The next year may look different as product teams learn to hide that machinery and make AI feel easier to use.
original: AI adoption is largely a product problem today.
most AI products look like airplane cockpits with 100 levers - connectors, permissions, model selection, token usage etc.
Things will look materially different in the next 12 months as product teams come into their own and make AI products easier to use.

rewrite: Madhu Guru 认为，今天 AI adoption 的核心其实是产品问题。即使在那一小部分愿意付费的人里，使用深度仍然很浅，因为很多产品把 connectors、permissions、model selection、token usage 等 100 个控制杆一股脑交给用户。
接下来一年，产品团队会逐渐学会把这些机械结构藏起来，让 AI 真正变得好用。
original: 今天，AI adoption 很大程度上是一个产品问题。
大多数 AI 产品看起来像有 100 个控制杆的飞机驾驶舱。
未来 12 个月，随着产品团队真正成熟，事情会明显不同，AI 产品会变得更容易使用。

rewrite: Thibault Sottiaux got to inbox zero for the first time by turning it into an active goal for his dot. The agent deleted unneeded email in batches, organized labels, surfaced messages needing replies and gathered context before he answered.
The interesting part is not inbox zero itself. It is the shift from asking AI one question at a time to giving it a concrete outcome to own.
original: I have never in my life achieved inbox zero until I just made it an active goal for my dot to help get it done.
delete all categories of email that were not needed for me to keep, validating them in batch
walked me through emails that needed a reply, searching for relevant context in the background

rewrite: Thibault Sottiaux 第一次做到 inbox zero，不是靠更努力地处理邮件，而是把它设成 dot 的主动目标。agent 批量删除不需要保留的邮件、整理标签、找出需要回复的消息，并在后台补齐上下文。
真正有意思的不是清空收件箱，而是工作方式变了：不再逐条问 AI，而是把一个明确结果交给它负责。
original: 我这辈子第一次做到 inbox zero，直到我把它设成 dot 要帮我完成的主动目标。
批量删除那些我不需要保留的邮件，并逐批确认。
带我过一遍需要回复的邮件，并在后台搜索相关上下文。

sections.title: Agent 还没有进入大多数工作 / Agents Have Not Reached Most Workflows
sections.desc: coding 已经跑起来了，但知识工作的下一波 adoption 需要重做流程、数据、责任与治理。

rewrite: Aaron Levie sees agent adoption as sharply bimodal: coding and coding-adjacent work has taken off, while most other knowledge work is still very early. Even inside coding, only a minority are running background agents in parallel; many developers still work with agents one-to-one.

The reason is structural. Real adoption requires workflows to be rebuilt, data wired differently, accountability and liability clarified, and governance, compliance and security upgraded. That is why the eventual opportunity may still be 100x larger than what we have seen.
original: AI agent adoption is still very bimodal right now. You have coding and coding adjacent tasks which have taken off, and then everything else.
most of the workflows still need to reengineered to work with agents.
you can basically expect 100X more agent adoption from what we’ve seen so far.

rewrite: Aaron Levie 看到的 agent adoption 呈现出明显的两极分化：coding 及其邻近任务已经起飞，其他知识工作还处在非常早期。即便在 coding 里，真正让 background agents 并行工作的也只是少数，大多数开发者仍然是和 agent 一对一协作。
原因不是大家没兴趣，而是工作流本身要重做，数据要重新接线，责任与问责要重新定义，治理、合规和安全也要升级。所以，今天看到的 adoption 可能还只是未来的 1%。
original: 现在 AI agent adoption 仍然非常两极化：coding 和 coding adjacent 任务已经起飞，其他一切还没有。
大多数工作流仍然需要重新设计，才能和 agent 一起工作。
你基本可以预期，agent adoption 最终会达到目前所见的 100 倍。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari points to a small but revealing agent battleground: Amazon appears to be protecting its ads business and brand, while DoorDash is slowly opening its ordering system through CLIs and text. Personal agents may make these distribution choices strategically important.
His other warning is simpler: explore the edges, but do not maximize tokens just for the sake of maximizing tokens.
original: It'll be interesting to see how this innovator's dilemma plays out in the next few years as personal agents become inevitable..
Amazon is protecting it's "ads" cash cow and *cough* the brand.
Doordash, albeit smaller, is opening the gates (slowly) with their CLIs and allowing to order via text.

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari 提到一个很小、但很能说明问题的 agent 战场：Amazon 似乎在保护广告业务和品牌，而 DoorDash 正通过 CLI 和文本下单，慢慢开放自己的系统。个人 agent 普及后，这种分发选择会变得越来越关键。
他的另一个提醒更简单：可以用 token 探索边界，但不要为了消耗 token 而消耗 token。
original: 随着 personal agents 成为必然，未来几年这个 innovator's dilemma 会怎么展开，很有意思。
Amazon 正在保护它的广告现金牛，以及，咳，它的品牌。
DoorDash 虽然更小，但正在通过 CLI 慢慢打开大门，允许用户用文本下单。

sections.title: AI 工厂的中间层 / The Operating System Between GPUs and Models
sections.desc: 真正的 AI 工厂不只是 GPU 堆起来，还要管理数据、模型、推理、权限和组织自己的 intelligence。

cards.authorTag: VAST Data CEO · The MAD Podcast

rewrite: The AI factory is not just a room full of GPUs. Renan Hallak describes a new infrastructure layer that has to manage compute, storage, networking, databases, training, inference and eventually teams of agents. The data is also changing: images, video, sound and natural language require much more space and much faster access than old enterprise workloads.

His sharper point is about ownership. As agents learn from an organization's experiences, that fine-tuned intelligence becomes IP. Enterprises may run models on-prem, in a colo or in an AI cloud, but they need to retain control of their data, weights, models and agents. The software infrastructure layer has to make that safe, including confidential inference where neither side sees what it should not see.

The memorable mental model: this layer is becoming the operating system for a new era, and eventually an intelligence marketplace may let organizations lease skills without exposing the underlying weights.
AI factory 不是简单地堆一屋子 GPU。Renan Hallak 描述的，是一层新的基础设施：它要管理 compute、storage、networking、database、training、inference，最终还要管理一组组 agent。数据本身也变了：图片、视频、声音和自然语言，比传统企业 workload 占空间更多，也需要更快的访问速度。
更锋利的判断在于 ownership。agent 从组织的真实经历中学习后，fine-tuned intelligence 会变成新的 IP。企业可以把模型放在 on-prem、colo 或 AI cloud，但必须掌握自己的数据、weights、models 和 agents。基础设施层要提供这种安全边界，包括让双方都看不到不该看到内容的 confidential inference。
他给出的记忆点是：这一层正在成为新时代的 operating system，未来甚至可能出现 intelligence marketplace，让组织租用技能，却不暴露底层 weights。

sections.title: 别让 AI 把所有人带到同一个平均值 / Do Not Converge to the Mean
sections.desc: 工具越能快速复制，个人视角和主动选择就越重要。

rewrite: Ryo Lu worries that AI makes convergence to the mean frictionless. We copy what works, measure what gets attention, then feed the result back into the next round until everything becomes polished, plausible and interchangeable.

His answer is to treat software more like an artistic medium. The important questions are not on a competitor's roadmap: what are you trying to make someone feel or understand, and what have you noticed that existing tools do not? If we can make almost anything, deciding what deserves to exist becomes the real work.
original: ai makes this loop frictionless.
a tidal wave of mid.
if we can make almost anything, deciding what deserves to exist becomes more important, not less.
what is the point of everyone being able to make something, if we all end up making the same thing?

rewrite: Ryo Lu 担心，AI 让“趋同到平均值”变得毫无摩擦：我们复制有效的东西，研究什么能得到注意，再把结果喂回下一轮，最后一切都变得 polished、plausible、interchangeable。
他的答案是把 software 当成一种艺术媒介。真正重要的问题不在 competitor roadmap 里：你想让别人感受到什么、理解什么？你注意到了什么，而现有工具还没有注意到？当几乎什么都能做时，决定什么值得存在，才是最难的工作。
original: AI 让这个循环变得毫无摩擦。
一股 mid 的潮水。
如果我们几乎什么都能做，那么决定什么值得存在就变得更重要，而不是更不重要。
如果每个人都能做出东西，结果却是我们都做出同一种东西，那又有什么意义？

rewrite: Sam Altman flags a different version of the same problem: he is uncomfortable with people treating AI models as having religious authority, or surrendering human judgment to them. He calls that a real safety issue.
Sam Altman 提醒的是同一个问题的另一面：他不舒服于人们把 AI model 当成具有宗教权威的东西，或者干脆把人的判断交出去。他认为这本身就是一个真实的 safety issue。

sections.title: 安全不是附加项 / Security Becomes a Core Function
sections.desc: 随着 agent 和 AI adversary 变强，安全会同时变成 verification、资源分配和创业机会。

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch expects security to become a larger function inside software companies. He frames it as both verification engineering, such as asking whether code is probably memory-safe, and capital allocation: deciding which attack surfaces deserve the most tokens.

For startups, increasingly capable AI adversaries make trust harder for tiny teams. But the same dependence on centralized systems and the poor state of cybersecurity also leave large areas open for small teams to disrupt.
Guillermo Rauch 预计，security 会在 software company 里变成更大的职能。它既是 verification engineering，比如判断代码是否大概率 memory-safe，也是 capital allocation：决定哪些 attack surface 最值得投入 token。
AI adversary 越来越强，小团队越难获得信任；但人们对中心化系统的依赖和糟糕的网络安全现状，也给小团队留下了大量可以突破的空间。
